newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Polifarb merger seen in Cieszyn's favour.
newsitem.headline: Polish Polifarb merger seen in Cieszyn's favour.

text.p: A compromise in a dispute on the planned merger between Polish paintmakers Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw might be reached in favour of the former's shareholders, a bourse official said.

Bourse supervisory board head Leszek Juchniewicz, currently mediating between the two firms' shareholders, told the daily Parkiet in its Thursday edition that a compromise resembling that proposed by Pioneer investment fund could be reached.
In March the Polish unit of the U.S.-based group pushed through a Cieszyn shareholder meeting a proposal upping Cieszyn's share in the new entity to 53.5 from 50 percent.
A month later the state treasury, a 16-percent Wroclaw shareholder, said Wroclaw shareholders should hold sway.

"A compromise can be worked out between Pioneer's proposal and the original merger plan which provides for an equal proportion (of shares)," Juchniewicz was quoted as saying, adding that a compromise would likely be reached.
He said that next week he would talk with state treasury officials on the matter.

Cieszyn currently has 19,125,000 shares, 2,978,820 fewer than Wroclaw, and a bonus issue of that number of shares in the original merger plan was meant to make up for the difference for each firm's shareholders to get half of the new entity.
Polifarb Cieszyn's 53.5 percent of the new firm would come about through a pre-merger bonus issue for them of 6.375 million shares.
The treasury ministry requested a bonus issue of 10 million shares to shift control of the planned new company in favour of Wroclaw's shareholders.
